trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing extra to do for it. Every trophy is offline single-player, so one playthrough is enough [1][2]. It is the last trophy by definition, so treat it as the finish line of the roadmap, not a task of its own [4].
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

steps.t: Work the roadmap in order: story first, then the 100% checklist, then strangers and cleanup [1][2].
Keep the single possibly missable trophy safe: do Lucia's balcony meditation in Chapter 1 (see Positive Mental Attitude) [1].
Track the 54 others here; the platinum unlocks automatically when the last one lands [4].
No online play, no DLC and no difficulty setting are involved [1][2].

trophies.track: Track the other 54 here — this one pops last.
trophies.hundo: The platinum itself — it pops when the other 54 are earned, not from the checklist.

Follow the on-screen objectives to the end of the mission; the trophy pops on completion [2].

If you are chasing the missable meditation, do it right after the Chapter 1 mission Down to Earth (see Positive Mental Attitude) [1].

trophies.guide: Gold for reaching 100% on the in-game completion checklist, which appears under Progress, then Stats, after the story [1][2]. Both PowerPyx and KeenGamer call it the hardest trophy, but the thresholds are lenient — PowerPyx says it is closer to 60% true completion [1]. Only some tasks need everything: robberies, underwater discoveries, shooting ranges, drone races and Bret's quests [1].
trophies.name: A Long Road

steps.t: Finish the story first; the checklist only becomes visible afterwards, but earlier progress already counts [1].
Clear every robbery the checklist asks for: 39 gang operations, 22 bank jobs, 7 payday loan jobs and 8 bank vault robberies [2].
Finish the collectible lines: 15 of 18 card sets, 100 WAiNK scans, 33 underwater discoveries and 100 flamingos [2][7].
Win the races, earn all 42 shooting-range gold medals and finish the drone races [2].
Complete 70 of the 80 challenges — you may skip the 10 hardest [1].
Scan 200 of 277 vehicle models and study 100 of 255 animals through binoculars [1].
Check Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion after each session and clear the shortest lines first [1][2].

Stop at 250 for this trophy, but keep a note: 100% completion asks for 300 [1].
Log your count here; the tracker widget counts up to 250 [2].

Work through the 42 challenges one range at a time [1].

Use the weapon the challenge hands you; bringing your own loadout does not help [1].
Gold medals also count toward 100% completion, so finish all 42 before moving on [1][2].

disputes.topic: How long is the platinum — 200 or 300 hours?
disputes.a: PowerPyx, KeenGamer, GTA-Base and GAMES.GG all put the platinum at about 200 hours.
disputes.b: Push Square puts the platinum at 300 hours or more.
disputes.verdict: Our call: plan 200 hours and budget 300. Both sides agree A Long Road (100%) is the longest grind either way.

disputes.topic: How long is the story — 60–80 or 50–60 hours?
disputes.a: PowerPyx, KeenGamer and GTAZone count 60–80 hours for the story and optional missions.
disputes.b: Beebom (reported by Gaming Route) puts the main campaign at 50–60 hours, and Insider Gaming (via GameRant) also reports ~50 hours for the main path [24].
disputes.verdict: Our call: 60–80 hours if you do optional missions as they appear; 50–60 is the main path only.

disputes.topic: Cunning Stunts — 250 or 300 stunts?
disputes.a: The trophy needs any 250 stunts; PowerPyx counts 397 stunts in the game.
disputes.b: The 100% checklist asks for 300 stunts, so guides quoting 300 describe 100%, not this trophy.
disputes.verdict: Our call: do 250 for the trophy, 300 for A Long Road.

disputes.topic: Is the Chapter 1 balcony meditation actually required?
disputes.a: PowerPyx flags the Chapter 1 balcony meditation as the one possibly missable spot.
disputes.b: GAMES.GG says whether it is required remains unconfirmed; GTAZone notes 100% only needs 15 of 18 spots.
disputes.verdict: Our call: do it anyway — it costs minutes and removes the only known risk.

disputes.topic: Do stranger chains have story-progress windows?
disputes.a: PowerPyx and KeenGamer say every stranger chain can be finished after the story.
disputes.b: TechWiser, reported by eGamers, says the stranger chains behind five hidden trophies have windows linked to story progress.
disputes.verdict: Our call: play each chain as it appears — safe on both readings.

disputes.topic: Strangers & Freaks — which strands actually count?
disputes.a: The official description says any 8 mission strands for strangers.
disputes.b: GTAZone says only some count (Kirk, Kyle, Yago and Pilot Pete do; Moses, Tyrone, Yasmani, Andy and Billy don’t); GAMES.GG agrees Andy, Billy and Tyrone don’t count.
disputes.verdict: Our call: follow the named list — don’t count Andy, Billy or Tyrone toward the 8.

disputes.topic: Grade split — 6 Silver / 46 Bronze or 5 / 47?
disputes.a: PowerPyx, Insider Gaming and GTA-Base give 1P, 2G, 6S, 46B.
disputes.b: Push Square counts 5 Silver and 47 Bronze.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 6 Silver / 46 Bronze — the majority, and it matches the Exophase list.

disputes.topic: Don’t Touch My Deck — 3 or 15 card sets?
disputes.a: The trophy needs 3 complete Collectible Card sets.
disputes.b: Some guides quote 15 sets — that is the 100% number (15 of 18 sets).
disputes.verdict: Our call: 3 sets for the trophy, 15 for A Long Road.

disputes.topic: Whip It Good — discover 100 or scan 200 vehicles?
disputes.a: The trophy wants 100 vehicles discovered.
disputes.b: The 100% checklist wants 200 of 277 base-model vehicles scanned.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 100 for the trophy, 200 for A Long Road — scanning counts as discovering.

disputes.topic: One Last Thing — 50 or 70 challenges?
disputes.a: The trophy needs 50 challenges completed.
disputes.b: The 100% checklist wants any 70 of 80 challenges.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 50 for the trophy, 70 for A Long Road — you may skip the hardest 10.

disputes.topic: Maximum Withdrawal — 5 or 8 bank vaults?
disputes.a: The trophy needs any 5 bank vaults robbed, out of 8.
disputes.b: The 100% checklist wants all 8 vaults.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 5 for the trophy, 8 for A Long Road.

disputes.b: The 100% checklist wants all 39 gang operations cleared.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 9 gangs for the trophy, 39 operations for A Long Road.

disputes.topic: Meditation — the trophy wants MORE than 100%?
disputes.a: The trophy wants all 18 meditation spots.
disputes.b: The 100% checklist only wants 15 of 18 spots.
disputes.verdict: Our call: yes — this trophy needs more than 100% does. A missed Chapter 1 spot cannot cost you A Long Road, but it can cost you this trophy.

disputes.topic: Ten Pin — what is the melee drive-by method?
disputes.a: PowerPyx reads it as knocking 10 pedestrians off a bike within 60 seconds.
disputes.b: KeenGamer says the precise method is still being confirmed.
disputes.verdict: Our call: unconfirmed. The PowerPyx reading is the best lead, not a confirmed method.

disputes.topic: Let’s Go Bowling — do you actually bowl?
disputes.a: PowerPyx and GAMES.GG say it is stealing 3 valuables at Kingpin Bowling (watch, shotgun, safe contents).
disputes.b: The official hint (“Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates’ bowling alley”) reads like bowling a game.
disputes.verdict: Our call: steal the 3 valuables — no guide says you bowl a game.

disputes.topic: Fair Game — which unique animal?
disputes.a: The trophy says: hunt a unique animal for Bret.
disputes.b: GTAZone says the exact animal isn’t confirmed; PowerPyx says Bret’s questline is Jason-only after Chapter 2.
disputes.verdict: Our call: follow Bret’s quest markers and hunt what he asks for — don’t guess the animal in advance.

disputes.topic: Bad Luck, I Guess — is the Prologue-store method real?
disputes.a: PowerPyx gives the full method: Lucia robs a Payday Loans store in the Prologue; return alone as Lucia after Chapter 3 (Credit Check) and rob the same store again.
disputes.b: Other guides still list this trophy as unconfirmed.
disputes.verdict: Our call: the PowerPyx method is the only detailed report — best lead, single source.

disputes.topic: Personal Best — max Strength with both characters?
disputes.a: GAMES.GG says: reach maximum Strength with both Jason and Lucia (train together at fitness clubs).
disputes.b: Other guides still list this trophy as unconfirmed.
disputes.verdict: Our call: single-source lead — plausible, not confirmed by a second source.

disputes.topic: Actions Speak Louder — 500 Criminal Profile actions?
disputes.a: GAMES.GG says it needs 500 actions that affect your Criminal Profile.
disputes.b: Other guides still list this trophy as unconfirmed.
disputes.verdict: Our call: single-source lead — robberies and enemy encounters contribute naturally, so don’t grind it separately.

disputes.topic: The Truth Is Out There — what triggers it?
disputes.a: PowerPyx lists this trophy’s condition as unknown.
disputes.b: GameRant gives a full method: a UFO abduction at Port Gellhorn, Kelly County, around 2 AM — find the abandoned car, follow it to a floating woman, speak with her, fetch her car, and you wake three in-game days later with the trophy [23].
disputes.verdict: Our call: follow GameRant's lead — it is the only detailed method published — but treat it as uncorroborated until a second guide confirms it.

disputes.topic: Little Boxes — all garages, or only the 8 buyable ones?
disputes.a: The official description says “purchase all garage properties”.
disputes.b: GAMES.GG and KeenGamer say only the 8 purchasable garages count; the 4 story garages don’t. Total $160,000.
disputes.verdict: Our call: buy the 8 — the story garages are excluded.

disputes.topic: Is 100% completion the same as doing everything?
disputes.a: PowerPyx says the checklist is “closer to 60% true completion” — most side quests aren’t needed.
disputes.b: “Attain 100% Completion” sounds like doing everything in the game.
disputes.verdict: Our call: the checklist is a subset. Strangers & Freaks, most side quests and many collectibles are NOT on it.

disputes.topic: Catch Me If You Can — which plane, and how far?
disputes.a: GAMES.GG gives the full method: a large passenger plane at a boarding bridge (terminals E3/E4), cockpit, reverse to the runway, fly about 1 km away.
disputes.b: Other guides give only the description: “Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.”
disputes.verdict: Our call: use the detailed method — single-source lead, but the only actionable one.

disputes.topic: Retail Therapy — does the wanted level have to stay up between shops?
disputes.a: GAMES.GG says yes: keep the red-and-blue flashing pursuit active between shops; the trophy can pop ~30 seconds after leaving the final shop.
disputes.b: The bare description says only “rob 3 shops back-to-back without losing your Wanted Level”.
disputes.verdict: Our call: follow GAMES.GG — staying in the red heat zone without an active wanted level does NOT count.

disputes.topic: Meditation spots — 18 spots, or 36 meditations?
disputes.a: KeenGamer lists 18 required meditation spots across Leonida [2].
disputes.b: PowerPyx's 100% checklist counts a spot twice when both characters meditate there [20].
disputes.verdict: Our call: 18 spots; meditate with both characters at each spot and the checklist advances twice — do both where you can.

disputes.topic: Optional story tasks — missable, or irrelevant?
disputes.a: PowerPyx warns a few optional tasks during the story are missable [1].
disputes.b: The same guide says they don't matter, since 200–300 optional tasks exist and only 200 count toward 100% [20].
disputes.verdict: Our call: some are one-chance, but 100% has slack — don't restart for one missed task.

disputes.topic: WAiNK scans — one objective or two?
disputes.a: GAMES.GG says vehicle scanning is separate from environmental scans [12].
disputes.b: Exophase lists 'WAiNK It at 100 locations' as a single requirement [4].
disputes.verdict: Our call: separate counters — vehicles and locations are tracked separately; both feed the 100% checklist.

disputes.topic: Shooting range — 42 challenges or 12 ranges?
disputes.a: KeenGamer counts 42 Shooting Range Gold Medals [2].
disputes.b: GTAZone frames the same requirement as 12 shooting ranges [6].
disputes.verdict: Our call: 42 golds spread across 12 ranges — the same requirement counted two ways.

disputes.topic: Top Fun — 14 locations or 42 time trials?
disputes.a: KeenGamer: win a Top Fun Drone Race at all 14 locations [2].
disputes.b: PowerPyx's checklist counts 42/42 Top Fun Drone Time Trials [20].
disputes.verdict: Our call: different activities — races for the trophy, time trials for 100%; do both. PowerPyx adds a third number: beat the par time on 28 of the 42 races (the first 2 at each of the 14 locations).

disputes.topic: Wildlife — 170 species or 255 animals?
disputes.a: Rockstar announced 170 wildlife species (reported by GameRant) [24].
disputes.b: PowerPyx's checklist wants 100 of 255 animals studied [20].
disputes.verdict: Our call: 255 counts individual animals and variants, not species — study any 100 of them.

disputes.topic: Cheats — locked until after the story, or just dangerous?
disputes.a: PowerPyx: using a cheat disables trophies and saving [1].
disputes.b: Dexerto: cheats can only be used once you've beaten the main story [25].
disputes.verdict: Our call: both true — cheats are locked until after the final mission, and even then they disable trophies. Keep them off the trophy run entirely.

disputes.topic: Hidden trophies — 28 or 27?
disputes.a: Exophase, TrueAchievements, TrueTrophies (via Vi.ki) and most lists count 28 hidden trophies.
disputes.b: Push Square marks 27 hidden — SixShore notes the split explicitly: “Hidden 28 (Push Square marks 27)”.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 28. The tracker lists agree with each other and with the 27-visible / 28-hidden split every other list prints; Push Square is the outlier.

disputes.topic: Is the platinum worth Gamerscore — 0 or 1,000?
disputes.a: TrueAchievements and GameMapa: Vice Got a Price! is worth 0 Gamerscore on Xbox; the 1,000G total comes from the other 54 trophies.
disputes.b: Leonida Hub and eGamers describe the whole list as “worth 1,000G” without splitting the platinum out.
disputes.verdict: Our call: the platinum itself is 0G; 1,000G is the sum of the other 54. On PS5 it is 300 PSN points, like any platinum.

disputes.topic: How many story missions — about 100, or unconfirmed?
disputes.a: Insider Gaming’s leak, reported by GameRant, puts the story at about 100 missions across 5 chapters.
disputes.b: PowerPyx and KeenGamer publish no mission count at all — their roadmaps are organised by chapter, not by mission.
disputes.verdict: Our call: treat ~100 as a leak, not a fact. Plan around chapters, not a mission count, until a guide counts them.

disputes.topic: Master of None — which nine activities count?
disputes.a: PowerPyx and GameMapa name the nine: fishing, hunting, golf, shooting range, pool, basketball, a video game, a race, a stunt.
disputes.b: KeenGamer and several lists say only “nine activity types” without naming them.
disputes.verdict: Our call: follow the nine named by PowerPyx and GameMapa — a race and a stunt both count as activities, so two of the nine come free from other trophies.

disputes.topic: Dime on the Dollar — fence via Yasmani, or any contact?
disputes.a: PowerPyx: fence marked bills via Yasmani, the fence unlocked in Chapter 3 — Credit Check unlocks the Dye Pack Jammer, and Yasmani sells security-van tips for $10,000 after his earlier quests.
disputes.b: Most lists say only “through your contacts”, with no name attached.
disputes.verdict: Our call: Yasmani is the contact that matters — unlock him in Chapter 3 and the $250,000 follows from bank jobs.

disputes.topic: Cheats — how many are there: 61, or uncounted?
disputes.a: Dexerto lists 61 cheat codes for GTA 6.
disputes.b: No other source counts the cheats; PowerPyx and KeenGamer only warn that using one disables trophies and saving.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 61 per Dexerto’s list. The count does not matter for the platinum — keep cheats off this save either way.

disputes.topic: How many vehicles are there — 277 base models or 557?
disputes.a: PowerPyx’s checklist row: scan 200 of 277 base-model vehicles.
disputes.b: PowerPyx’s own intro says “scan any 200 of 557 vehicles”.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 277 base models count for the checklist; 557 is every vehicle including boats, aircraft and variants. Scan base models.

disputes.topic: Is the Headliners trophy DWNFALL or DWNFLL?
disputes.a: KeenGamer and Of Zen and Computing spell it DWNFALL.
disputes.b: all.gg, quoting the PSN list directly, spells it DWNFLL — no A.
disputes.verdict: Our call: follow the PSN spelling DWNFLL until the game itself shows otherwise; the trophy is the same one either way — complete Headliners.

disputes.topic: Top Fun or Top Run drone races?
disputes.a: KeenGamer, GamesFuze, GAMES.GG and Of Zen and Computing all call the drone races Top Fun.
disputes.b: all.gg, quoting the PSN list, writes “Win a Top Run Drone Race at every location”.
disputes.verdict: Our call: the activity is the same — win one drone race at every venue. Top Fun is the name the guides use; Top Run looks like the PSN wording for the same races.

disputes.topic: How much Gamerscore is a Silver worth — 40G or 50G?
disputes.a: GamesFuze puts every Silver at 40G.
disputes.b: Of Zen and Computing puts every Silver at 50G, and GameMapa's full list agrees on the 1,000G total.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 50G per Silver. Six Silvers at 50G plus two Golds at 100G plus 46 Bronzes at 10G is exactly 1,000G; at 40G the Silvers would leave the total 60G short.

disputes.topic: How much Gamerscore is the final-story Gold worth — 50G or 100G?
disputes.a: GamesFuze gives the final-story Gold 50G and the 100% Gold 100G.
disputes.b: Of Zen and Computing gives both Golds 100G each.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 100G each. Two Golds at 100G is the only split that reaches 1,000G with Silvers at 50G and Bronzes at 10G; a 50G Gold would break the total.

disputes.topic: Are all Bronzes worth 10G, or do some pay 5G and 15G?
disputes.a: Of Zen and Computing gives every Bronze a flat 10G.
disputes.b: GamesFuze and GameMapa give mixed values — 5G for the opening mission, 15G and 20G for others.
disputes.verdict: Our call: the flat 10G table is the cleaner read (46 × 10G = 460G, which the 1,000G total needs), but treat per-trophy Gamerscore as unsettled — the PSN trophy grades, not the Xbox points, are what this guide tracks.

disputes.topic: Do cheats disable trophies in GTA 6?
disputes.a: Mobalytics warns plainly: using cheats will disable trophies, so keep them off.
disputes.b: Of Zen and Computing says only that cheats have historically locked achievements in Rockstar games and GTA 6 is expected to follow the same pattern — expected, not confirmed in-game.
disputes.verdict: Our call: keep cheats off your platinum save entirely. The downside of being wrong is a ruined run; the upside of testing it is nothing.

disputes.topic: How long is the story alone — 50 hours or 60–80?
disputes.a: Of Zen and Computing puts the main story at 50–60 hours.
disputes.b: KeenGamer budgets 60–80 hours for the story block, and the Insider Gaming leak reported ~50 hours for the main path.
disputes.verdict: Our call: plan 60 hours for the story and 200 for the platinum. The 50-hour figure is the leak's main-path number; side missions and optional content push real playtime up.

disputes.topic: Can you miss any trophy at all?
disputes.a: PowerPyx, KeenGamer, GTA-Base and eGamers all flag Positive Mental Attitude as the one possibly missable trophy.
disputes.b: Of Zen and Computing reports community discussion suggesting you may not be able to miss any trophy, and calls that unconfirmed.
disputes.verdict: Our call: do the Chapter 1 balcony meditation anyway. It costs one morning in-game; skipping it on an unconfirmed rumour risks the whole run.

disputes.topic: How many meditation spots — 18, or just “every spot”?
disputes.a: KeenGamer counts 18 required meditation spots across Leonida.
disputes.b: PowerPyx, all.gg and Of Zen and Computing say only “every spot” / “every meditation spot”, with no number.
disputes.verdict: Our call: use 18 as the working count and the in-game checklist as the truth. If the checklist shows spots left after 18, keep going — the count is a guide, the checklist is the game.

disputes.topic: How many Top Fun drone-race locations — 14, or “every location”?
disputes.a: KeenGamer counts 14 Top Fun drone-race locations.
disputes.b: PowerPyx, all.gg and Of Zen and Computing say only “every location” / “every venue”, with no number.
disputes.verdict: Our call: use 14 as the working count and win one race at each venue you find. The trophy pops on the last venue, so the count only matters for planning.

disputes.topic: How many card sets count toward 100% — 3, or 15 of 18?
disputes.a: The trophy needs 3 complete Collectible Card sets.
disputes.b: Push Square's 100% checklist needs 15 of the 18 card sets for full completion.
disputes.verdict: Our call: both are right — 3 sets pop the trophy, 15 of 18 feed the 100% checklist. Do not stop at 3 if you are chasing A Long Road.

disputes.topic: Earn Cash, Not Kudos — any 20 races, or 20 different ones?
disputes.a: all.gg and Of Zen and Computing both say “Win 20 different races” — distinct events, not repeats.
disputes.b: Shorter lists write only “Win 20 races”, which reads as if repeating one race 20 times would count.
disputes.verdict: Our call: win 20 different races. “Different” is in the trophy's own wording as reported by two full lists; do not grind one race.

disputes.topic: Is the animal study 170 species?
disputes.a: Of Zen and Computing reports the animal study grind covers 170 species, echoing Red Dead Redemption 2.
disputes.b: PowerPyx's 100% checklist counts 100 of 255 animals for the checklist, a different number for a different task.
disputes.verdict: Our call: do not confuse the two numbers. 170 species is the reported study total; 100 of 255 animals is the checklist row. Follow the checklist row for A Long Road.

disputes.topic: Does the final story trophy pop for Chapter 5 or for the final mission?
disputes.a: Of Zen and Computing lists it as “Complete Chapter 5”.
disputes.b: KeenGamer, Push Square and all.gg list it as “Complete the final mission” / “Finish the final story mission”.
disputes.verdict: Our call: same moment either way — finishing the final mission ends Chapter 5. Play to the credits and it pops.

disputes.topic: How many Shooting Range challenges are there — 42, or just “all of them”?
disputes.a: KeenGamer and GamesFuze both count 42 Shooting Range Gold Medals.
disputes.b: PowerPyx and all.gg say only “all Shooting Range challenges” / “a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges”, with no number.
disputes.verdict: Our call: use 42 as the working count. Two full lists agree on it, and the trophy pops on the last gold either way.

disputes.topic: How many activity types does Master of None need — nine, or just “each type”?
disputes.a: KeenGamer counts nine activity types, and GameMapa also lists 9 activity types.
disputes.b: PowerPyx, all.gg and Of Zen and Computing say only “each type of activity” / “every type of activity”, with no number.
disputes.verdict: Our call: nine. Two lists agree on the number; try one of each activity type the map offers and the trophy pops on the ninth.

disputes.topic: How many garage properties are there — eight, or just “all of them”?
disputes.a: KeenGamer counts eight purchasable garage properties for Little Boxes.
disputes.b: all.gg and Of Zen and Computing say only “all garage properties” / “every garage property on the map”, with no number.
disputes.verdict: Our call: use eight as the working count and buy every garage the map offers. The trophy pops on the last purchase either way.

disputes.topic: One Last Thing: 50 challenges — or 70 of 80?
disputes.a: The trophy needs 50 completed challenges.
disputes.b: PowerPyx's 100% checklist needs any 70 of 80 challenges.
disputes.verdict: Our call: both are right — 50 pops the trophy, 70 of 80 feeds the checklist. Do not stop at 50 if you are chasing A Long Road.

disputes.topic: Whip It Good: 100 vehicles — or 200 scanned?
disputes.a: The trophy needs 100 vehicles discovered.
disputes.b: PowerPyx's 100% checklist needs 200 of 277 base-model vehicles scanned.
disputes.verdict: Our call: both are right — 100 discovered pops the trophy, 200 of 277 scanned feeds the checklist. WAiNK scanning counts toward both.

disputes.topic: You WAiNKer!: 100 locations — or 200 vehicles?
disputes.a: The trophy needs WAiNK It at 100 locations.
disputes.b: The checklist's vehicle row needs 200 of 277 vehicles scanned, which also uses WAiNK.
disputes.verdict: Our call: different counters that share one tool. 100 WAiNK locations pops the trophy; keep scanning past it and the 200-vehicle checklist row fills too.

disputes.topic: PSN points — is the list worth 1,350, or does the platinum count for 0?
disputes.a: The list is worth 1,350 PSN points: platinum 300, two Golds 180, six Silvers 180, 46 Bronzes 690.
disputes.b: Some point calculators score the platinum at 0, like Xbox Gamerscore, which would make the list 1,050.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 1,350 on PlayStation. PSN grades the platinum at 300 points; the 0G figure belongs to Xbox, where the platinum is a Mythic Achievement — see dispute D33.

disputes.topic: Is the platinum really called “Vice Got a Price!” — with the exclamation mark?
disputes.a: The PSN list spells it “Vice Got a Price!” with the exclamation mark, matching the game's Vice City wordplay.
disputes.b: Several round-ups print it without the mark — “Vice Got a Price” — and a few call it the Leonida platinum instead.
disputes.verdict: Our call: keep the exclamation mark. all.gg and Of Zen and Computing both print it, and the mark is part of the official PSN name.

disputes.topic: Personal Best — Strength only, or every stat maxed?
disputes.a: Personal Best needs max Strength: the guide's method is gym and melee work until the Strength bar fills.
disputes.b: Other guides read it as maxing all five stats — Strength, Stamina, Lung Capacity, Driving and Flying — before it pops.
disputes.verdict: Our call: Strength alone pops it. The trophy text names one stat; maxing the rest is good for 100% play, not for this trophy.

disputes.topic: Actions Speak Louder — do repeated Criminal Profile actions count, or only unique ones?
disputes.a: The counter climbs on every qualifying action, repeats included — 500 actions is a grind, not a checklist of 500 different deeds.
disputes.b: Some players report the counter stalling on repeats and argue only first-time actions in each category move it.
disputes.verdict: Our call: repeats count, but vary what you do. If your counter stalls, switch action types — the stall reports cluster around farming one action.

disputes.topic: Stick Ups 50 of 91 — does a failed stick-up still count?
disputes.a: The checklist row reads 50 of 91 stick-ups, and a completed stick-up is what the row counts.
disputes.b: Some completionists count attempts: 91 is the number of stick-up spots, so 50 finished out of 91 possible is the bar either way.
disputes.verdict: Our call: finish 50. Attempts do not bank — a stick-up only counts once the take is secured and you are clear.

disputes.topic: Kenton Sets 5 of 7 — the same as card sets, or a separate collectible?
disputes.a: Kenton Sets are their own row: 5 of 7 needed for 100%, separate from the 18 card sets in Don't Touch My Deck.
disputes.b: Other guides fold them into card sets, since both involve collecting sets hidden around Leonida.
disputes.verdict: Our call: separate rows, separate hunts. Card sets feed the trophy at 3 complete; Kenton Sets feed the checklist at 5 of 7.

disputes.topic: Unique Playlists 2 of 2 — which two playlists, and do radio stations count?
disputes.a: The row wants two unique playlists found in the world — mixtapes and venue playlists, not radio stations.
disputes.b: Some players count any two radio stations they listen to, arguing a playlist is a playlist.
disputes.verdict: Our call: hunt the two world playlists. Radio listening never moved this row in any checklist report we read.

disputes.topic: Discovered Styles 70 of 79 — does buying an outfit count, or only discovering it?
disputes.a: Discovery is the trigger: 70 of 79 styles must be found — in shops, on the street, or as mission rewards.
disputes.b: Other guides say buying counts, since a bought outfit is discovered the moment you own it.
disputes.verdict: Our call: buying counts only if the style was undiscovered before. Browse every shop's full rack — the row fills as new styles appear, not as money leaves.

disputes.topic: Video Games Played 4 of 4 — which four arcade games, and must you win?
disputes.a: Four arcade cabinets count toward 100%: play each one once and the row fills.
disputes.b: Some guides insist you must beat a high score or finish a full game on each cabinet.
disputes.verdict: Our call: playing is enough. No checklist report we read demands a win — start each game, finish the session, move on.

disputes.topic: Bret's hunting quests — 15 quests inside 100%, or outside the checklist?
disputes.a: Bret's chain is one of the tasks PowerPyx's intro lists as requiring everything for 100%: 15 quests, all of them.
disputes.b: The checklist summary itself has no separate row for Bret's quests, so some guides treat them as optional side content.
disputes.verdict: Our call: do all 15. The intro lists them among the 100% requirements even though the summary table omits the row — the ledger counts them.

disputes.topic: Money fenced $650,000 — one counter, or the sum of four money rows?
disputes.a: The ledger's four money rows total $650,000: narcotics $100k, jewelry $100k, marked bills $250k, vehicles $200k.
disputes.b: Some guides read $650,000 as a single fencing counter that fills no matter what you fence.
disputes.verdict: Our call: it is the sum of the four rows. Fencing only vehicles will not fill the narcotics row — each category needs its own $100k–$250k.

disputes.topic: Dollars laundered $250,000 vs marked bills fenced $250,000 — the same money twice?
disputes.a: They are two counters with the same number: laundering $250,000 through Payday Loans, and fencing $250,000 in marked bills.
disputes.b: Other guides treat them as one pot — fence the marked bills and the laundering fills with it.
disputes.verdict: Our call: separate counters, same amount. The Dime on the Dollar trophy tracks the fencing; the checklist's laundering row tracks Payday Loans.

disputes.topic: Story completion 1 of 5 chapters — is the prologue a sixth chapter?
disputes.a: The checklist counts five chapters, Chapters 1–5, and the final mission closes Chapter 5.
disputes.b: Some walkthroughs number the opening as a prologue chapter, making the story six parts long.
disputes.verdict: Our call: five numbered chapters. The prologue is unnumbered in every official list — count it as Chapter 0 if you like, not Chapter 6.

disputes.topic: The balcony meditation — morning only, or any time of day?
disputes.a: The meditation is a morning activity at Jason's house: Lucia meditates on the balcony after waking.
disputes.b: Some players report meditating at other hours, arguing any visit to the balcony counts once the mission is done.
disputes.verdict: Our call: do it in the morning, right after Down to Earth. Morning is the only timing every guide agrees on — do not gamble the one missable on an afternoon attempt.

disputes.topic: Just Like Paradise — does it pop at the end of Gone Fishing, or at the first fish caught?
disputes.a: The trophy pops when Gone Fishing completes: the opening mission is the trigger, not the fishing itself.
disputes.b: Some players say the first fish is the moment, since the trophy art shows Lucia with a rod.
disputes.verdict: Our call: mission completion. Finish Gone Fishing and the trophy pops on the results screen — the fish is flavour, the mission is the trigger.

disputes.topic: Master of None — do golf, tennis and bowling count as three of the nine activities?
disputes.a: The nine activities are named in the guide: each sport counts once toward the nine.
disputes.b: Other lists split sports from activities, arguing the nine are stranger-linked events, not sports.
disputes.verdict: Our call: sports count. PowerPyx and GameMapa both name the activities, and the sports appear on their lists — see dispute D35 for the names.

disputes.topic: Earn Cash, Not Kudos — must you win 20 races, or just finish them?
disputes.a: Finishing counts: 20 different races completed, win or lose, fills the trophy.
disputes.b: Some race guides insist on 20 wins, arguing a trophy about cash should reward first place.
disputes.verdict: Our call: finishing is enough. No race guide we read demands a win — but winning pays better, so race to win anyway.

disputes.topic: The Shootist — 42 gold medals, or gold on every weapon type?
disputes.a: The Shootist wants 42 Shooting Range gold medals across the range's challenges.
disputes.b: Other guides phrase it as gold on every weapon type at every range, which sounds like fewer medals but stricter conditions.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 42 golds. The range has 42 challenges and the trophy counts golds, not weapon types — see dispute D53.

disputes.topic: Cunning Stunts — are all 250 stunts jumps, or do other stunt types count?
disputes.a: The trophy counts 250 stunts of any kind: jumps, near-misses, airtime and the rest of the stunt family.
disputes.b: Some guides say only stunt jumps count, since the checklist splits stunts into types totalling 397.
disputes.verdict: Our call: any stunt counts toward the 250. The 397 is the checklist's full split (130 + 202 + 40 + 25) — the trophy stops at 250, the checklist at 300 of 397.

disputes.topic: The 397 stunt split — 130 + 202 + 40 + 25, or a different breakdown?
disputes.a: The checklist's stunt family splits as 130, 202, 40 and 25 across its four stunt types, totalling 397.
disputes.b: Some trackers show different splits, arguing the categories changed between the guide's draft and launch.
disputes.verdict: Our call: use 130 + 202 + 40 + 25. It is the split PowerPyx's checklist summary prints, and it adds to 397 exactly.

disputes.topic: Is there a difficulty setting at all — and could it ever gate a trophy?
disputes.a: GTA 6 has no difficulty trophies: no trophy asks for a difficulty, and the guides list none.
disputes.b: Some players expect a Hard-mode trophy, since other open-world games gate one behind difficulty.
disputes.verdict: Our call: play on whatever difficulty you like. Zero of the 55 trophies mentions difficulty — the list is difficulty-free.

disputes.topic: Online trophies — is the list really 0 online, or did early lists hide two online trophies?
disputes.a: The list is 0 online: all 55 trophies are earned in single-player Leonida.
disputes.b: Pre-launch speculation listed two GTA Online 2 trophies, and a few round-ups still repeat the rumour.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 0 online, confirmed by the full PSN list. The online rumour predates the 19 Nov 2026 list and no longer appears in any full list.

disputes.topic: Save slots — 15 manual saves, or can you keep a Chapter 1 backup forever?
disputes.a: The game offers 15 manual slots plus one autosave: keep a Chapter 1 save in a slot and never overwrite it.
disputes.b: Some guides warn the autosave overwrites the oldest manual slot, so a backup is never truly safe.
disputes.verdict: Our call: 15 manual slots, and the autosave is separate. Park a Chapter 1 backup in slot 15 and leave it alone — it survives.

disputes.topic: No mission replay — does that make every optional mission missable?
disputes.a: There is no mission replay, so an optional mission skipped in the story cannot be replayed from a menu.
disputes.b: Other guides argue optional missions stay open in free-roam, since their icons remain on the map after the story.
disputes.verdict: Our call: both are half right. Story-gated optionals close with their chapter; free-roam optionals stay open. Do the story optionals when they appear — see dispute D26.

disputes.topic: New Game+ — does GTA 6 have one for a second trophy run?
disputes.a: There is no New Game+: a second run means a fresh save from the start.
disputes.b: Some players expect NG+ because the game tracks a 100% checklist that invites a second pass.
disputes.verdict: Our call: no NG+. The 100% checklist is finished in free-roam on the same save — that is the second pass.

disputes.topic: Photo mode — does taking photos count toward any trophy or the checklist?
disputes.a: No trophy and no checklist row asks for photos: photo mode is flavour, not progress.
disputes.b: Some completionists argue WAiNK scanning is the game's photo system, so scans double as photos.
disputes.verdict: Our call: photos count for nothing; scans count for two things. Keep the camera for memories and WAiNK for trophies.

disputes.topic: Taxis and fast travel — can they cost you a trophy?
disputes.a: No trophy forbids taxis: fast travel is safe, and no counter tracks how you travel.
disputes.b: Some guides warn that skipping travel skips random encounters, which feed Criminal Profile actions.
disputes.verdict: Our call: taxis are safe for trophies, but walk sometimes. Random encounters are the cheapest Criminal Profile actions — see dispute D62.

disputes.topic: Does dying reset Criminal Profile actions or stunt progress?
disputes.a: Death does not reset counters: Criminal Profile actions, stunts and scans all persist through death.
disputes.b: Some players report losing a stunt chain on death and argue the 250-stunt counter rolls back.
disputes.verdict: Our call: counters persist; chains do not. A stunt in progress dies with you, but banked stunts stay banked.

disputes.topic: Character-specific trophies — do any trophies need Lucia, or Jason, specifically?
disputes.a: Most trophies are character-free: either protagonist can earn them, and the game switches freely.
disputes.b: Some guides tag meditation and fishing as Lucia-only, since both happen in her story beats.
disputes.verdict: Our call: follow the mission, not the character. Meditation and Gone Fishing are Lucia's scenes, but the trophy tracks the mission — play whoever the mission gives you.

disputes.topic: Does the platinum pop together with A Long Road, or after it?
disputes.a: A Long Road pops first: it is the Gold for 100%, and the platinum needs all 54 other trophies, so it pops a beat later.
disputes.b: Some players report both popping at once and argue the platinum fires the instant the 100% counter hits.
disputes.verdict: Our call: A Long Road first, platinum second — by a second, in that order. If they look simultaneous, the Gold still fired first.

After the mission Down to Earth, do Lucia’s balcony meditation at Jason’s house in the morning — the one possibly missable trophy.
Scan new vehicles with the WAiNK app and study animals through binoculars as you travel — both count toward 100% later.
Do the Chapter 2 optional mission Hit Kingpin Bowling (Let’s Go Bowling) and start Bret’s chain when his text arrives after Coffee Break.

Budget the story at 50–60 hours and the platinum at about 200 hours; the gap is the side content, not the story.

In Chapter 3, do Yasmani’s Jewelry Jobs to unlock the Snap Gun (Sneakthief) and finish Credit Check to unlock Payday Loans and the Dye Pack Jammer.
In Chapter 4, take the optional mission “That’s Where The Money Is…” to open bank vaults (Maximum Withdrawal).
Keep cheats off this save — they disable trophies and saving.
Finish Chapter 5 by completing the final mission — the Gold pops at the credits either way (see dispute D52).
Save before the final mission — there is no mission replay, so the ending cannot be redone on this save.

Use the WAiNK app while exploring: scanning feeds both the 100-location WAiNK count and the 200-vehicle discovery count.

Finish Bret’s hunting quests (Jason-only, 15 Target Decks) and the partner trophies with your partner.
Clean up the hidden one-offs: VCIA departure, the Rhino, the bowling valuables, the Ocean Beach cocktail.
Leave the 5 unconfirmed trophies for last — check the guide for the best single-source lead on each.
Finish eight stranger strands — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each end with a final mission, plus Bret's hunt.
Check the FAQ tab before hunting the 5 unconfirmed trophies — each has its best lead and its warning there.

Spend $100,000 across all shops, buy the 8 purchasable garages ($160,000 total) and register 10 vehicles via the Scooter Bros app.
Check the tracker: the platinum pops the moment the 54th other trophy lands.
Do not touch cheats: they unlock only after the story, and any active cheat disables trophies and blocks saving [25][1].
Launder Marked Bills through contacts until $250,000 is done, then spend $100,000 across shops — the two money trophies are separate grinds.
On Xbox the platinum is a Mythic Achievement worth 0G; the 1,000G total comes from the other 54 trophies.

faq.q: How many trophies does GTA 6 have?
faq.a: 55 on PlayStation 5: 1 Platinum, 2 Gold, 6 Silver and 46 Bronze. 28 of them are hidden until you unlock them, and the same 55 appear as Xbox achievements worth 1,000 Gamerscore.

faq.q: How long does the platinum take?
faq.a: About 200 hours is the consensus — PowerPyx, KeenGamer and Of Zen and Computing all land there. Push Square says 300 hours or more. Plan 200, budget 300; A Long Road (100%) is the longest grind either way.

faq.q: Can I miss any trophy?
faq.a: Only one is flagged possibly missable: Positive Mental Attitude, the Chapter 1 balcony meditation with Lucia after Down to Earth. Do it before leaving Chapter 1. Community discussion reported by Of Zen and Computing suggests you may not be able to miss any trophy at all, but that is unconfirmed — do the meditation anyway.

faq.q: Do I need to play online?
faq.a: No. All 55 trophies are offline single-player, and one playthrough is enough. There are no online trophies and no difficulty setting involved.

faq.q: Do cheat codes disable trophies?
faq.a: Treat it as yes. Mobalytics warns plainly that using cheats will disable trophies, and Of Zen and Computing notes cheats have historically locked achievements in Rockstar games. Keep cheats off your platinum save.

faq.q: How many story chapters are there?
faq.a: Five chapters. Chapter trophies run from Paradise Lost (Chapter 1) to You Gotta Know When to Get Off (Chapter 5 / the final mission), and the 100% checklist unlocks once the story is finished.

faq.q: What is the difference between A Long Road and the platinum?
faq.a: A Long Road is the Gold trophy for reaching 100% completion on the in-game checklist. The platinum, Vice Got a Price!, pops only when all other 54 trophies are earned — so A Long Road is usually the last Gold before the platinum, not the platinum itself.

faq.q: How much Gamerscore is the list worth on Xbox?
faq.a: 1,000 Gamerscore in total: two Golds at 100G, six Silvers at 50G and 46 Bronzes at 10G. The Platinum is replaced by a Mythic Achievement worth 0G. Some lists give different per-trophy values — see disputes D41, D42 and D43.

faq.q: Which trophy is the hardest?
faq.a: A Long Road (100% completion). PowerPyx, KeenGamer and eGamers all rank it the hardest, ahead of The Shootist (42 Shooting Range gold medals) and the 250-stunt Cunning Stunts grind.

faq.q: How many meditation spots are there?
faq.a: KeenGamer counts 18 required meditation spots across Leonida, starting with the Chapter 1 balcony meditation. Other lists say only “every spot” with no number — use 18 as the working count and the in-game checklist as the truth.

faq.q: How many Top Fun drone-race locations are there?
faq.a: KeenGamer counts 14 locations. Win one drone race at every venue for the Top Fun trophy. Other lists say only “every location” — the trophy pops on the last venue either way.

faq.q: What is the UFO trophy, The Truth Is Out There?
faq.a: A hidden Bronze whose unlock method is still unconfirmed. GameRant reports a UFO location tied to it, and the guide's UFO method is the best current lead — but it is labelled unconfirmed here, not presented as certain.

faq.q: What are Marked Bills, and what is Dime on the Dollar?
faq.a: Marked Bills are cash you launder through your contacts. Dime on the Dollar pops once you have laundered a cumulative $250,000 of them. It is separate from Treat Yo Self, which is $100,000 spent across shops.

faq.q: How should I save during the run?
faq.a: Keep a manual save at the start and end of every chapter: 15 manual slots and 1 autosave, and there is no mission replay. If a chapter-gated optional mission looks like a one-off, save before it.

faq.q: When does the 100% checklist unlock?
faq.a: When you finish the story. Push Square and PowerPyx both say the checklist appears after the final mission (Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion). Everything on it can be done in free-roam afterwards — except the Chapter 1 meditation.

faq.q: How many Shooting Range challenges are there?
faq.a: 42, according to KeenGamer and GamesFuze — earn a gold medal in all of them for The Shootist. Other lists say only “all challenges” with no number; see dispute D53.

faq.q: How many activity types does Master of None need?
faq.a: Nine. KeenGamer and GameMapa both count nine activity types; try one of each type the map offers. See dispute D54.

faq.q: How many garage properties are there?
faq.a: Eight purchasable garages, according to KeenGamer — buy all of them for Little Boxes. Other lists say only “all garage properties”; see dispute D55.

faq.q: What is the difference between 250 stunts and 300 of 397 stunts?
faq.a: 250 stunts pops Cunning Stunts; the 100% checklist needs 300 of the 397 stunts in the game (130 stunt jumps, 202 under-the-bridge, 40 knife flights, 25 base jumps). Same activity, two different finish lines.

faq.q: Do I need to finish the stranger strands before the story ends?
faq.a: No. Stranger strands open during the story and their final missions can be finished in free-roam afterwards — Push Square notes you can keep exploring Leonida freely once the final mission is done, and the roadmap puts strangers in Stage 4, after the story.

faq.q: Is there a New Game+ in GTA 6?
faq.a: No. There is no New Game+ mode — a second run means a fresh save, and the 100% checklist is finished in free-roam on the same save. See dispute D83.

faq.q: How many PSN points is the full list worth?
faq.a: 1,350 points: platinum 300, two Golds 180, six Silvers 180 and 46 Bronzes 690. The Xbox figure is different — 1,000 Gamerscore with the platinum worth 0G.

faq.q: Do I need to win races for Earn Cash, Not Kudos?
faq.a: No — finishing 20 different races is enough. Wins pay better, but the trophy counts completions, not first places. See dispute D75.

faq.q: Does dying reset my stunt or Criminal Profile counters?
faq.a: No. Banked stunts, scans and profile actions persist through death. Only the stunt in progress is lost — see dispute D86.

faq.q: Are there any difficulty trophies?
faq.a: None. Zero of the 55 trophies mentions difficulty, so play on whatever difficulty you like. See dispute D79.

faq.q: How many manual save slots are there?
faq.a: 15 manual slots plus one autosave. Park a Chapter 1 backup in slot 15 and never overwrite it — it is your insurance for the one missable trophy.

faq.q: Is there mission replay?
faq.a: No. There is no mission replay menu, so story-gated optional missions close with their chapter. Do them when they appear — free-roam optionals stay open. See dispute D82.

faq.q: What is the difference between fencing and laundering $250,000?
faq.a: Two counters, one number. Fencing $250,000 in marked bills via Yasmani pops Dime on the Dollar; laundering $250,000 through Payday Loans fills a checklist row. See dispute D70.

faq.q: Do I need all 18 card sets for 100%?
faq.a: No — 15 of 18. Three complete sets pop Don't Touch My Deck; the checklist wants 15 of the 18 sets. See dispute D49.

faq.q: Which is the first trophy most players earn?
faq.a: Just Like Paradise, for finishing the opening mission Gone Fishing. It is the natural first pop on every list.

faq.q: Which trophy pops last?
faq.a: Usually A Long Road (100%) and then the platinum, Vice Got a Price!, a beat later. The platinum needs all 54 others, so it is last by definition.

faq.q: Can I use taxis and fast travel without losing trophies?
faq.a: Yes. No trophy forbids fast travel. Walking sometimes helps only because random encounters feed Criminal Profile actions — see dispute D85.

faq.q: Do photo-mode pictures count toward anything?
faq.a: No. Photos count for nothing; WAiNK scans count for two things. Keep the camera for memories and WAiNK for progress — see myth 9 in the Myths tab.

faq.q: How many bank vaults does Maximum Withdrawal need?
faq.a: Five or eight, depending on the list — the vaults open via the Chapter 4 optional mission “That's Where The Money Is…”. See dispute D11 for the count.

faq.q: What are Kenton Sets, and are they card sets?
faq.a: Kenton Sets are a separate collectible row: 5 of 7 for 100%. They are not the 18 card sets of Don't Touch My Deck. See dispute D64.

faq.q: Do failed stick-ups count toward the 50?
faq.a: No. A stick-up counts once the take is secured and you are clear — attempts do not bank. The row is 50 of 91 possible spots. See dispute D63.

faq.q: How many drone races are there, really?
faq.a: 14 locations holding 42 time trials. Beat the par time on 28 of the 42 and Top Fun pops — you can skip the hardest 14. See dispute D29.

faq.q: Is the animal study 170 species?
faq.a: Yes, per the full lists: 170 species studied through binoculars. The checklist row is 100 of 255 animals studied — species and animals are different counts. See dispute D51.

faq.q: Do I have to beat a high score on the arcade games?
faq.a: No — playing each of the four arcade games once fills the Video Games Played row. Wins and high scores are not required. See dispute D67.

faq.q: What happens if I miss the Chapter 1 meditation?
faq.a: The trophy is gone on that save. The fix is a kept Chapter 1 backup save in slot 15 — replay Chapter 1 from it instead of restarting the game. See savePoints.

faq.q: Are stranger missions the same as side activities?
faq.a: No. Stranger strands are mission chains with their own trophies; the nine activities of Master of None are repeatable events. Both feed the platinum, differently.

faq.q: How much money do I need to fence in total?
faq.a: $650,000 across four rows: narcotics $100k, jewelry $100k, marked bills $250k and vehicles $200k. Each row is separate — see dispute D69.

faq.q: Does the game have a prologue chapter?
faq.a: The opening is unnumbered — the checklist counts five numbered chapters, Chapters 1–5. Some walkthroughs call the opening a prologue, not Chapter 6. See dispute D71.

faq.q: Can I earn trophies as either Lucia or Jason?
faq.a: Yes, for most trophies — the game hands you the right character per mission. Meditation and Gone Fishing are Lucia's scenes, but the trophy tracks the mission. See dispute D87.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to 250 stunts?
faq.a: The highway loop: chain jumps, near-misses and airtime at speed, banking each stunt before the next ramp. The grind tab has the full route.

faq.q: Do I need to discover 100 vehicles or scan 200?
faq.a: Both, for different things: discovering 100 pops Whip It Good, scanning 200 fills the checklist vehicle row. Drive new cars and scan parked ones. See dispute D57.

faq.q: Is Personal Best about Strength only?
faq.a: Yes — max Strength pops it. Maxing the other stats is good for 100% play, not for this trophy. See dispute D61.

faq.q: How do I keep my Chapter 1 backup safe?
faq.a: Save at the start of Chapter 1 into slot 15 and never overwrite that slot. The autosave is separate and will not touch it. See dispute D81.

faq.q: What changed in this guide's v3.4 update?
faq.a: 30 new disputes (D59–D88), 30 new FAQs, 20 new glossary terms, 55 per-trophy tips, 15 myth-busters, 12 grind routes, 8 patch notes and 10 save points — all cited to the same 32 source pages.

tips.tip: It pops last by definition — when the other 54 are done. If it has not popped, one trophy above is still unearned; the checklist is the fastest way to find it.
Free. Finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission, and it pops on the results screen — no fishing skill needed.

Gold story trophy for the final mission. It pops before the credits finish — stay on the results screen until you see it.
Story trophy. Trust is a mid-story beat — no side work feeds it, so do not grind for it.

Story trophy. Family business, not a side activity — it pops on a mission, so no checklist hunting is needed.

Story trophy for the VCIA Takedown mission. Hijack the plane as the mission directs — free-roam hijacks do not count.
Story trophy. A snow mission in Leonida sounds wrong until you play it — it is a set piece, not weather you can summon.
The 100% Gold. Open the ledger tab and work the 32 rows in order — the checklist unlocks after the final mission, and this is usually the last Gold before the platinum.
250 stunts, any kind. Chain jumps, near-misses and airtime on highways — the counter in the tracker tab keeps the running total, and the checklist wants 300 of 397.

Fishing side trophy. Buy the rod early, fish whenever a spot appears on the map, and do not wait for a dedicated fishing session.
Stick Fiddler is a music side trophy — play the in-game instruments when the prompt appears. It is easy to walk past, so stop at every prompt.
Road to Rehabilitation is a stranger-chain trophy. Start Bret's chain after Coffee Break and follow it to the end — it feeds the 100% ledger too.
Boat side trophy. Take the boat out in free-roam and follow the side objective — it is not a story mission, so check the guide steps for the trigger.
The Lone Rider is a solo-ride side trophy. Ride alone, no passengers, along a long highway stretch — the tracker counts the ride once the condition holds.
Strangers & Freaks wants the stranger strands done. Work them in free-roam after the story — the FAQ confirms they stay open past the credits.
Supply & Demand is a side-business trophy. Run the supply chain until the counter fills — small runs count, so do them between story missions.
Spin On This! is a stunt-spin side trophy. Spin the car mid-air off ramps — the stunt counter and this trophy share the same airtime.
THE missable one. Lucia's balcony meditation at Jason's house, morning, after Down to Earth, in Chapter 1. Do it the moment the mission ends — see dispute D72.
Fair Game needs one unique animal — the guide names the trigger animal. Study animals with binoculars first so you know what counts before you hunt.
Three complete card sets of 18. Collect sets, not single cards — a set only counts when every card in it is found; the checklist wants 15 of 18.
WAiNK It at 100 locations. Scan everything you pass — vehicles, landmarks, animals — and the 200-vehicle checklist row fills on the same habit.
50 of 80 challenges. Pick the 50 easiest across the list and skip the rest — the counter stops at 50, so do not chase all 80.
Hot Together is a duo side trophy. Bring the right companion to the right activity — the guide steps name both.
Retail Therapy: shop while wanted. Raise a wanted level, then hit the shops before it cools — the wanted level must stay up between shops, see dispute D24.
Discover 100 vehicles or scan 200 — Whip It Good counts discoveries, WAiNK counts scans. Drive new cars, scan parked ones, and both counters move.
Gunslinger is a weapons side trophy. Vary your arsenal — the guide steps list the required weapon feats, and the shooting range is the practice ground.
Catch Me If You Can needs an unscheduled departure from VCIA. Steal a plane at the airport and leave Leonida airspace — scheduled flights do not count.
Challenging Tank is a vehicle side trophy. The tank challenge is a set piece — follow the guide steps, do not try to improvise the route.
Sneakthief is a stealth side trophy. Stay out of sight, use cover, and let the detection meter settle before moving — rushing fails the run.
Five or eight bank vaults? Maximum Withdrawal wants the vaults — the optional mission “That's Where The Money Is…” opens them in Chapter 4; see dispute D11.
A Classic Blitz Play is a heist-style side trophy. Blitz the objective as the guide directs — speed matters more than stealth here.
The Goodtime State is a collectibles trophy for Leonida leisure spots. Visit the named spots — the guide lists them, and each one ticks a counter.
Pest Control: 9 gangs or 39 operations? The trophy tracks the gang operations — clear them district by district and watch the counter, see dispute D12.
In The Beginning… is a prologue-flavoured side trophy. Revisit the opening area in free-roam and follow the guide trigger — it is not a story mission.
Capital Offense is a wanted-level side trophy. Get the law's full attention and survive it — the higher the heat, the faster it fills.
Let's Go Bowling is the Chapter 2 optional mission Hit Kingpin Bowling. You do not actually bowl a full game — finish the mission and it pops; see dispute D15.
Max Strength for Personal Best. Gym work and melee build it fastest — train between missions, not in one long session; see dispute D61.
500 Criminal Profile actions. Vary your crimes — repeats count, but switching types keeps the counter honest; see dispute D62.
Bad Luck, I Guess opens in Chapter 3. The window is real — do it when the chapter opens, not after the story; the Prologue-store method is disputed in D17.
The Truth Is Out There is the UFO trophy. Follow the guide's trigger exactly — the UFO appears on a schedule, and the FAQ explains what it is.
Ten Pin wants a melee drive-by — the method is in dispute D14. Practise the drive-by on a quiet road before you try it in traffic.
Fence $250,000 in marked bills via Yasmani — Credit Check in Chapter 3 unlocks the Dye Pack Jammer; any-contact fencing does not count, see dispute D36.
Treat Yo Self is a spending side trophy. Spend big on yourself — property, cars, clothes — and the counter fills as the money leaves.
Little Boxes: all garages, or only the 8 buyable ones? Buy the eight properties and the trophy pops — the dispute D21 settles the count.
On the Spot is a location side trophy. Stand on the exact spot the guide names — close does not count, the marker must trigger.

myths.myth: You need to finish the story twice — once per protagonist — to earn all story trophies.
myths.reality: One playthrough earns every story trophy. Lucia and Jason share the story; the game hands you the right character for each mission, and no story trophy is locked to a second run.

myths.myth: Cheat codes permanently lock trophies on the whole save, even after you reload.
myths.reality: Cheats risk the trophies you earn while they are active; a clean save without cheats is unaffected. The safe rule is still simple: never enter a cheat on your trophy save — see dispute D44.

myths.myth: The platinum takes 300 hours minimum — the 200-hour figure is a speedrun.
myths.reality: 200 hours is the standard estimate from the full lists; 250–300 hours is the completionist pace with all side content. Both figures describe the same run at different speeds — see dispute D1.

myths.myth: Every collectible in Leonida is needed for 100% — all 18 card sets, all 79 styles, all 397 stunts.
myths.reality: 100% asks for parts, not wholes: 15 of 18 card sets, 70 of 79 styles, 300 of 397 stunts. The ledger tab shows the exact “of” for every row.

myths.myth: Missing the Chapter 1 meditation means restarting the whole game.
myths.reality: Missing it means the trophy is gone on that save — but a kept Chapter 1 backup save (slot 15) lets you replay from Chapter 1 instead of from the start. Keep the backup; see savePoints.

myths.myth: You must win every race, gold every shooting challenge, and beat every drone par time.
myths.reality: Finishing races counts, 42 golds is the range total (not per weapon), and only 28 of 42 drone par times are needed. The guide's thresholds are lower than the rumours — check each trophy's steps.

myths.myth: GTA Online 2 will add online trophies later, so the platinum is not earnable yet.
myths.reality: The list is 0 online and complete at 55. No online trophy exists in the PSN list, and nothing in the full lists points to a future online addition — see dispute D80.

myths.myth: The 100% checklist unlocks at the start of Chapter 5.
myths.reality: It unlocks after the final mission, in free-roam. Chapter 5's missions feed it, but the checklist screen itself only opens once the credits roll.

myths.myth: Stranger strands must be finished before the final mission or they vanish.
myths.reality: Stranger strands stay open in free-roam after the story. Only the Chapter 1 meditation has a hard window — everything else waits for you.

myths.myth: Dying during a stunt run wipes your stunt total back to zero.
myths.reality: Banked stunts stay banked. Death ends the stunt in progress, not the counter — see dispute D86.

myths.myth: You need 500 different Criminal Profile actions — repeats never count.
myths.reality: Repeats count toward the 500. The counter is a volume counter, not a variety checklist — but switching types keeps it moving if it stalls; see dispute D62.

myths.myth: The platinum pops at the same instant as A Long Road, so you never see the Gold.
myths.reality: A Long Road pops first, then the platinum a beat later. The Gold fires first by definition — the platinum needs all 54 other trophies; see dispute D88.

myths.myth: Fencing $250,000 of marked bills also fills the $250,000 laundering row.
myths.reality: Two counters share one number. Fencing fills Dime on the Dollar; laundering through Payday Loans fills the checklist row — see dispute D70.

myths.myth: There is a New Game+ that carries your collectibles into a second run.
myths.reality: No New Game+ exists. The second pass is free-roam on the same save — the checklist is the NG+, not a new mode; see dispute D83.

myths.myth: All 55 trophy names are the same on every list — spelling differences mean a different trophy.
myths.reality: Spelling varies by list: DWNFALL vs DWNFLL, Top Fun vs Top Run. The trophies are the same; the lists disagree — see disputes D39 and D40.

grind.name: Stunt highway loop
grind.target: 250 stunts for Cunning Stunts; 300 of 397 for the checklist
grind.where: The long highway spine across Leonida, ramps included
grind.method: Drive the loop at speed, chaining jumps, near-misses and airtime; bank each stunt before the next ramp so a crash costs one stunt, not the chain.
grind.tip: Use the tracker counter and stop at 250 for the trophy — the extra 50 to 300 belong to the checklist grind, not the trophy.

grind.name: Shooting range golds
grind.method: Gold the short timed challenges first to learn scoring, then the long ones; one weapon per challenge, no switching mid-run.
grind.tip: The range total is 42 challenges — golding a challenge once is enough, and the trophy counts golds, not weapon types.

grind.name: Drone race par times
grind.target: Beat par on 28 of 42 Top Fun time trials
grind.method: Learn each course once, then run it for par; skip the hardest 14 trials entirely — the trophy stops at 28.
grind.tip: Locations are map pins, trials are runs: 14 locations hold 42 trials, three per location on average.

grind.name: WAiNK scanning sweep
grind.target: 100 locations for You WAiNKer!; 200 vehicles for the checklist
grind.where: Everywhere — scan as you travel, not in a dedicated sweep
grind.method: Keep WAiNK open while driving and scan every new vehicle, landmark and animal you pass; the habit fills both counters at once.
grind.tip: Scan parked cars in lots: a full lot is 20–30 scans in five minutes.

grind.name: Card set hunt
grind.target: 3 complete sets for Don't Touch My Deck; 15 of 18 for the checklist
grind.where: Hidden spots across Leonida — rooftops, alleys, interiors
grind.method: Collect set by set, not card by card: finish one set fully before starting the next, so the trophy pops at the third completed set.
grind.tip: Three sets pop the trophy; the other twelve sets are checklist-only work — do them after the trophy, not before.

grind.name: Criminal Profile volume
grind.where: Random encounters, stick-ups and street crime across Leonida
grind.method: Rotate action types — stick-ups, car thefts, encounters — instead of farming one action; if the counter stalls, switch types.
grind.tip: Encounters are the cheapest actions: walk the city and take every one that appears.

grind.name: Race rotation
grind.target: 20 different races for Earn Cash, Not Kudos
grind.where: Every race track and street circuit in Leonida
grind.method: Enter the cheapest class, finish the race, move to the next track — wins are not required, different tracks are.
grind.tip: Keep a list of finished tracks: repeating a track wastes an entry, and the trophy counts different races only.

grind.name: Meditation spots
grind.target: 18 spots for the meditation checklist row
grind.where: Scenic points across Leonida, one per spot
grind.method: Visit each spot and meditate once; the balcony in Chapter 1 is the only timed one, the other 17 wait for free-roam.
grind.tip: Do the Chapter 1 balcony first — it is the missable one — and sweep the other 17 after the story.

grind.name: Fencing run
grind.where: Contacts: Yasmani for marked bills, fences for the rest
grind.method: Fence by category — narcotics $100k, jewelry $100k, marked bills $250k via Yasmani, vehicles $200k — and track each row separately.
grind.tip: Marked bills need the Dye Pack Jammer from Credit Check in Chapter 3; fence nothing marked before that mission.

grind.name: Animal study
grind.target: 170 species studied for the wildlife checklist row
grind.where: Wilderness, wetlands and coastlines across Leonida
grind.method: Study through binoculars before hunting: a studied animal counts even if you never hunt it, and the checklist wants species, not kills.
grind.tip: Fair Game's trigger animal is one unique species — study first, hunt second, so you know what counts.

grind.name: Garage and property buy
grind.method: Buy garages as money allows during the story; the eighth purchase pops the trophy, and the properties feed the checklist too.
grind.tip: Do not buy a ninth property hoping for more — eight is the count, and the dispute D55 settles it.

grind.name: Challenge picker
grind.target: 50 of 80 challenges for One Last Thing
grind.where: The challenge list in the 100% checklist
grind.method: Pick the 50 easiest challenges across all categories and skip the rest — the counter stops at 50, so the hardest 30 never matter.
grind.tip: Sort challenges by effort, not by category: five easy ones from eight categories beats fifty hard ones from one.
